title: One pass, several things to remember
idea: TOOL (multiple state variables): a single walk through data can keep more than one running value at once - a total AND a count, side by side.

exercises.prompt: So far you kept ONE running value while walking a list - like a total. Some problems need to remember TWO things at once, like a total AND how many items. What lets you do that?
options: Keep two running variables, updating both each turn
Only one variable is ever allowed
You must walk the list twice, once per value
exercises.explanation: You just use more than one running variable. Each turn of the loop updates every one you care about. That is this unit's new tool: multiple state variables.

exercises.prompt: A single loop can update a running total AND a running count on the same turn.
exercises.explanation: Yes. One pass can carry several running values. Each turn you add to the total and add one to the count.

exercises.prompt: Why keep two running values in ONE loop instead of looping twice?
options: It reads the data once and stays in step - both values describe the same items
It is the only way Python allows
exercises.explanation: One pass keeps the values in step and only reads the data once. Both numbers describe the exact same items you walked.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

total = 0
count = 0
for n in [4, 6, 10]:
    total = total + n
    count = count + 1
print(total, count)
exercises.explanation: total grows 4, 10, 20; count grows 1, 2, 3. Two running values finish at 20 and 3 - printed together.

exercises.prompt: In that loop, what is the job of 'count = count + 1'?
options: Add one each turn so count remembers HOW MANY items were seen
exercises.explanation: count = count + 1 bumps the counter by one every turn, so it ends up holding the number of items.

exercises.prompt: Both running variables must be set to their starting values BEFORE the loop begins.
exercises.explanation: Yes - total = 0 and count = 0 before the loop. If you start them inside, they would reset every turn and never accumulate.

exercises.prompt: What everyday task keeps two running values at once?
options: Totalling a shopping bill WHILE counting how many items go in the basket
exercises.explanation: A cashier adds to the bill and counts items at the same time - two running values, one pass down the counter.

exercises.prompt: Order the shape of a two-state loop.
blocks: Start BOTH running values before the loop
Each turn, update every running value
After the loop, use the finished values
exercises.explanation: Start both, update both every turn, then read both at the end. Same shape as one-state, just more of it.
high tracks the biggest (ends 90), low tracks the smallest (ends 30). Two trackers in one pass.

options: Keeping several running values through one pass over the data
exercises.explanation: Multiple state variables: track a total and a count, or a biggest and a smallest, all in one walk. No new syntax - just more running values.
